adjudication_label: Sources of oxygen ingress during processing
canonical_question: Is the increase in oxygen content from 0.65 wt% to 0.80 wt% during HIP due to surface oxidation during heating or bulk diffusion from residual oxides?

question_variants.question: Is the increase in oxygen content from 0.65 wt% to 0.80 wt% during HIP due to surface oxidation during heating or bulk diffusion from residual oxides?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence confirms the oxygen content increase to ~0.80 wt% during HIP but does not explicitly distinguish between surface oxidation during heating and bulk diffusion from residual oxides as the specific mechanism.

answers.answer: The text states that HIP caused a significant increase in oxygen content up to ~0.80 wt%, but does not specify if this is due to surface oxidation or bulk diffusion from residual oxides.
answers.mechanism: Unspecified between surface oxidation and bulk diffusion
answers.boundary_limitation: No mechanistic distinction provided in the text
evidence_spans: Very high hardness of the MA-SPS-HPT specimen (584 HV10) can be ascribed to the high oxygen content in solid solution and also the presence of oxide particles that caused additional strengthening.
As seen in Figure 8 hardness was correlated with oxygen content in the sample.
It should be pointed out that the MA-SPS-HPT specimen was broken into several pieces during the HPT process and therefore the results of such specimen are disputable.

source_evidence_spans: HIP caused even more significant increase in the oxygen content, up to ~0.80 wt %.
